prompt.context: You are presented with financial data for three anonymous companies — Company A, Company B, and Company C.
prompt.question: Here is information about Companies A, B, and C. What can you make of this data? And can you determine what type of industry each one is in?

clarifying_info.q: Can I calculate the Current Ratio?
clarifying_info.a: No — the data shows Total Assets and Total Liabilities, not Current Assets and Current Liabilities, so Current Ratio cannot be calculated.

exhibits.title: Financial Data for Companies A, B, and C
exhibits.shows: A table of five financial line items for three anonymous companies

framework: Compute key financial ratios for each company: ROA, ROE, Net Profit Margin, Debt-to-Assets, Debt-to-Equity
Interpret the ratio profile of each company relative to the others
Map the ratio pattern to an industry archetype (high-margin/low-volume vs. low-margin/high-volume vs. highly-leveraged financial institution)
State a recommended industry or company type for each, and explain the reasoning

questions.prompt: Calculate ROA, ROE, Net Profit Margin, Debt-to-Assets, and Debt-to-Equity for each company.
questions.guidance: Use Net Income / Assets for ROA, Net Income / Equity for ROE, Net Income / Revenue for Net Profit Margin, Liabilities / Assets for Debt-to-Assets, Liabilities / Equity for Debt-to-Equity. Current Ratio cannot be computed because only totals are given.

math.setup: Formulas: ROA = Net Income / Assets; ROE = Net Income / Equity; Net Profit Margin = Net Income / Revenue; Debt-to-Assets = Liabilities / Assets; Debt-to-Equity = Liabilities / Equity
math.answer: Co. A: ROA 9%, ROE 14%, NPM 10%, D/A 36%, D/E 56%. Co. B: ROA 1%, ROE 20%, NPM 9%, D/A 97%, D/E 3103%. Co. C: ROA 7%, ROE 18%, NPM 3%, D/A 60%, D/E 148%.

questions.prompt: Based on the ratios, what type of industry or company is each one likely to be?
questions.guidance: Co. A: highest ROA and NPM but lowest leverage — consistent with a low-volume, high-margin specialty retailer (e.g., luxury goods / jewelry). Co. B: near-zero ROA, extreme leverage (assets ≈ liabilities), very high ROE driven by leverage — classic hallmarks of a financial institution (bank or investment bank). Co. C: lowest NPM with high revenues and assets roughly twice liabilities — consistent with a high-volume, low-margin mass retailer.

recommendation: Co. A is most likely a low-volume, high-margin specialty retailer — the ratio profile matches a luxury/jewelry store (actual company: Tiffany & Co.).

Co. B is most likely a financial institution — extreme leverage with assets nearly equal to liabilities and very high ROE driven by debt are defining characteristics of a bank or investment bank (actual company: Morgan Stanley).

Co. C is most likely a high-volume, low-margin mass retailer — thin profit margins on enormous revenues with a more balanced asset/liability structure point to a large-scale retailer (actual company: Walmart).
risks: Ratio analysis alone cannot definitively identify an industry without additional context such as business description or segment data.
Leverage ratios for financial firms are structurally very high and not directly comparable to non-financial companies — this distinction is key to identifying Co. B.
next_steps: If additional data were available, examine current vs. long-term asset/liability splits, gross margin, and inventory turnover to further validate the industry classifications.
For a financial institution, examine net interest margin and Tier 1 capital ratios as more relevant metrics.
